Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Bee/wasp sting to right arm a few minutes prior to consult → local erythematous rash, puncture mark, no significant swelling observed.  
  • Subjective mild breathing difficulty and tingling/swelling sensation of right lip/tongue at onset; breathing normal on video exam.  
  • Past medical history: eczema.  
  • Drug allergy: penicillin.  
  • Occasional anxiety/panic attacks (never medicated).  
  • No previous anaphylaxis; never prescribed an EpiPen.
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • None currently taken.  
  • Advised: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet PO, up to 6 ×/day as needed, or any once-daily non-sedating antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Occasional anxiety; no current treatment; no self-harm risk discussed.
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Lives alone; employed as a computer scientist; pet cat at home.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Lips, oral cavity, and posterior pharynx visualized via video; no swelling or airway compromise noted.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not performed.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not applicable / Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Reassured patient that current presentation suggests localized allergic reaction rather than anaphylaxis.  
- Education: reviewed danger signs of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, stridor, increasing breathing difficulty); provided information link.  
- Medication: start OTC antihistamine as above.  
- Safety-netting: if breathing worsens, lip/tongue swelling develops, or rash spreads/becomes hot, attend ED immediately or contact clinic.  
- Monitor arm for signs of secondary infection; consider oral antibiotics if cellulitis develops.  
- No allergy testing required now; consider if future recurrent reactions.  
- No referrals booked; patient advised to re-contact if concerns arise.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (BP, HR), height/weight/BMI, waist circumference, full immunisation review, alcohol/smoking/substance use history, diet and exercise assessment, hearing and vision screening, formal mental health screening, urinalysis, baseline blood tests (BGL/lipids), STI screening, family medical history.  
● Internal contradictions: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear with minimal extraneous dialogue; no major audio gaps, but limited routine history and examination captured.
